sources_note: Primary source: sources/dragonsword/ static snapshot of https://dragonsword.site (53 HTML pages, fact-checked + independently reviewed per the task brief) — all hero/achievement/mechanic entities are a structural reorganization of that content; no field states a fact absent from the snapshot. Table-driven data (the 60-achievement list, the 17 named-boss list, the 19-hero tier-list grades, the 19-hero roster kit/ailment table, the 6-archetype comparison, the 19-hero unlock-planner classification) was extracted directly from each page's raw HTML <table>/<li> markup and spot-checked against a second, independent manual read of the same page. Steam's public endpoints (store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids=4570720, steamcommunity.com/stats/4570720/achievements/) were queried live on 2026-09-21 purely to sanity-check methodology (see delivery notes) — the live numbers were NOT written into any entity field, since the site's own guides/achievements page already carries a dated, methodologically-explained snapshot (2026-09-01) for every achievement, which is what this file uses throughout. This game (DragonSword: Awakening, Hound13 Inc., Steam appid 4570720) has no Chinese-language content anywhere on the site (config/hub.json marks it 'langs: EN'), so no name_zh-style fields were added (unlike data/valheim/entities.json, which mirrors a bilingual site) — every hero/achievement name here is the single English name the site itself uses; no translation was invented or needed. Universal caveat carried once here rather than in each of the 60 achievement entities: the achievements page states 'we do not know what denominator Valve uses' for its global-unlock-rate percentages, so every unlock_rate_pct field in this file is a fact about Steam's stats page on the stated date, not a directly comparable measure of 'how far a typical player gets' — that inference belongs to the reader, not this data.

hero-unlock-economy.name: Hero Unlock Economy (Story vs. Exchange)
hero-unlock-economy.summary: All 19 launch heroes are earned by playing — no gacha, no paid characters, no drop chance. Story heroes join as the campaign progresses; the rest are bought in the Exchange for a flat single Fate's Invitation each, regardless of hero. Money buys only cosmetics (costumes/Familiars), never heroes.
hero-unlock-economy.exchange_cost_per_hero: 1 Fate's Invitation (flat — every Exchange hero costs the same, no per-hero pricing, no shards)

status-ailments-and-signals.name: Status Ailments & Signal Skills (combat loop)
status-ailments-and-signals.summary: Core combat loop: Active Skills apply a Status Ailment -> a Signal Skill arms on whichever hero responds to that ailment -> switching to that hero fires the Signal as they tag in -> repeat. Signal Skills have no cooldown; arming is the only gate. Teams need overlapping ailment coverage, not complementary damage.
status-ailments-and-signals.ailments_confirmed_note: Nine are individually attested across store text, patch notes and hero descriptions; Hound13 has never published a canonical/complete list. Poison rests on a single passing player comment.
status-ailments-and-signals.difficulty_note: Content offers selectable difficulty tiers up to Very Hard, Nightmare and Extreme; rises automatically with Mercenary Corps rank and can be manually lowered.
status-ailments-and-signals.element_gate_note: Some enemies (e.g. Soulwarden Zemoor) take no damage at all until struck with the correct element; the game signposts this in the environment. Shock and Burn are the only two elements this site confirms actually bypass such an immunity.
status-ailments-and-signals.not_documented: No cleanse, resist stat or immunity system is described by any source this site considers reliable. No per-ailment build-up thresholds, durations or stack counts are published. Which Signal Skill responds to which ailment is never published — players are told to read each hero's own skill text in-game.
unverified_fields: three internal disagreements the ailment-coverage page names itself: (1) Kalsion carries no ailment in the roster data, but the Kalsion build guide classifies him as a Burn applicator/finisher; (2) Reina likewise carries none, but the build guide describes her as having an Airborne kit; (3) Aria is recorded as applying Fire, but the build guide says Burn for her

whether same-element-different-label pairs (Aria's Fire vs Kalien's Burn; Othello's Ice vs Dana's Freeze; Ornette's Electrocution vs Tarte's Shock) actually arm the same Signal is unconfirmed in all three cases

awakening-system.name: Awakening System
awakening-system.summary: Every hero has six Awakening levels. Each level is unlocked with a Stigma Awakened Stone, and each Stone costs 200 Fragments of Sacred Light (farmed mainly from Sudden Missions). Awakening changes a hero's playstyle/kit rather than only scaling stat numbers.
awakening-system.fragment_source: Sudden Mission completions (surprise mini-boss fights / timed challenges encountered while exploring)

only_named_per_hero_effect.note: The only per-hero Awakening effect published anywhere on this site, for any of the 19 heroes.

awakening-system.recommended_spending_order: Reach level cap and first Breakthrough before investing in Awakening; spread Stones across the active team rather than maxing one favourite hero.
awakening-system.cap_note: Patch 1.0.9 (13 Aug 2026) explicitly unlocked Lute, Johnny and Kalien up to their 6th Awakening — they were capped below the system's ceiling for the first three weeks after launch.
awakening-system.expansion_note: Hound13 stated on the 14 August All Day Live Q&A that the six-tier system 'is designed as-is' and further expansion 'isn't planned near-term'.
awakening-system.history_note: An earlier page on this site (Gear, Runes and Karma, 2026-08-12) hedged Awakening as 'at least three tiers, reportedly six' from two disagreeing player guides; the dedicated Awakening System page (2026-09-10) resolves this to a definitive six via a bylined Destructoid source. Not treated as a live conflict since the newer page explicitly narrates the resolution.
unverified_fields: what each of the six Awakening levels changes, for each of the 19 heroes, is published for exactly one hero (Theresia, level 1) — the other 18 heroes and the remaining 5 levels are undocumented
whether the Stigma Awakened Stone exchange rate or the 200-fragment cost changed in any patch after 24 July 2026 could not be confirmed

difficulty-and-boss-clear-verbs.name: Difficulty Tiers & Boss Clear Verbs (Subduer / Conqueror)
difficulty-and-boss-clear-verbs.summary: Difficulty rises automatically with Mercenary Corps rank and can be manually lowered; content offers selectable tiers up to Very Hard, Nightmare and Extreme. The only two difficulty names that appear anywhere in Steam's achievement text are Very Hard and Nightmare, split across two boss-achievement verbs: 'Subduer of X' (defeat 3 times, repeatable) and 'Conqueror of X' (defeat once, on a named difficulty).
difficulty-and-boss-clear-verbs.difficulty_tiers_note: 'Very Hard', 'Nightmare' and 'Extreme' are named as selectable content tiers on the combat guide; only 'Very Hard' and 'Nightmare' actually appear in achievement text (no boss is gated on 'Extreme' in any achievement).

conqueror_bosses.boss: Furcas, the Starving Ghost of Corrosion
The Earthlander of the Ravenous Earth

difficulty-and-boss-clear-verbs.note_on_verb_meaning: 'Subduer of X' = 'Defeated X 3 times' (repeatable world/field content). 'Conqueror of X' = one clear on the named difficulty. Unlock rate should not be read as a difficulty score — it measures how many people attempted a fight as well as how many won.
difficulty-and-boss-clear-verbs.hagen_counter: Hagen the Dark Necromancer is the only one of the 17 bosses with a published, citable counter: break the glowing decoy dummy he leaves behind before his expelled ghost returns, so he swaps into the knocked-down dummy instead of healing. Source: player Steam guide by 'Cat' (1,556 unique visitors), not Hound13.
unverified_fields: no HP, damage, resistance or phase-timer values are published for any of the 17 bosses by Hound13 or any source this site considers reliable
which named bosses are 'World Bosses' versus 'Hunt Monsters' is not published — the game distinguishes the categories but no source sorts the 17 into them
whether the Very Hard 'Ursula' boss achievement and the separately-confirmed 'Ursula Raid' are the same encounter at different scale, or two fights sharing a name, is not stated by any source

team-archetypes.name: Team Archetypes Compared
team-archetypes.summary: Six team archetypes recur in community discussion. This site can staff four of the six with named heroes from sourced material; Summon and Defensive Control remain unverified as lineups.

archetypes.name: Aerial
archetypes.core_mechanic: Airborne-launching heroes chain into each other; the most self-sufficient of the six
archetypes.heroes_confirmed: Astria, Eileen, Aria (all apply Airborne per Heroes: All 19); Roxy's 3rd-Awakening repeatable Air Stomps also fit the archetype

archetypes.name: Burn
archetypes.core_mechanic: Fire application into a Burn finisher
archetypes.heroes_confirmed: Kalsion, Aria, Kalien (per Kalsion build guide and Heroes: All 19); Reina named as a mixed-element partner
archetypes.sourcing_strength: Best-documented of the six — Kalsion is S-tier on both tracked tier lists

archetypes.name: Bleed
archetypes.heroes_confirmed: Theresia confirmed as the primary applier (Best Team Comps, Heroes: All 19); which heroes respond to her Bleed is explicitly unconfirmed
archetypes.sourcing_strength: Partial — one applier named, no full lineup

archetypes.name: Shock
archetypes.core_mechanic: Electrocution application, useful against element-gated enemies
archetypes.heroes_confirmed: Ornette (Electrocution, per Heroes: All 19); the incoming roadmap hero Ryza is described as shock-specialized on the patch notes and roadmap page but has not shipped
archetypes.sourcing_strength: Partial — applier named, payoff hero not identified in any source we have

archetypes.name: Summon
archetypes.core_mechanic: Built around a hero's summoned unit rather than a shared ailment
archetypes.heroes_confirmed: Not itemized anywhere on this site. Dana summons Chako (an ice golem) and Sion places a field Relic, per Heroes: All 19, but no source describes either as anchoring a "Summon team" specifically
archetypes.sourcing_strength: Unverified as a lineup — named by our combat guide as a recurring archetype, with no hero list behind it

archetypes.name: Defensive Control
archetypes.core_mechanic: Built around crowd control and survival rather than damage
archetypes.heroes_confirmed: Not itemized anywhere on this site
archetypes.sourcing_strength: Unverified as a lineup — same caveat as Summon

team-archetypes.unstaffed_note: Dana (summons Chako) and Sion (places a Relic) are the two heroes whose kits most resemble a 'Summon' identity, but no source frames either as anchoring a dedicated Summon team the way Kalsion is framed for Burn. No source names any Defensive Control lineup at all.
unverified_fields: no ranked comparison of the six archetypes against each other, and no numbers showing one archetype outperforms another in a specific fight, exist on this site

known_conflicts.topic: Achievement unlock-rate snapshots disagree across two site pages
known_conflicts.note: guides/achievements (dated 2026-09-01, used as this file's canonical achievement source) and guides/achievement-tracker (a separate tool page that 'refreshes weekly'; its own body text cites both '7 September 2026' and '2026-09-14' as capture dates in different paragraphs, and its numbers differ from the achievements page, e.g. 'Lucky!' 45.9% vs 46.4%-46.5%) never agree, and the tracker page's own internal capture-date references are inconsistent with each other. Expected drift over time, per the site's own methodology note ('these numbers move, including ours') — not treated as a value conflict on any single achievement entity, but flagged here since the tracker page's internal dates alone do not agree.
